questions.subject: JAVASCRIPT
questions.learningObjective: Interpret JavaScript behavior demonstrated by a short executable snippet involving arrays — reduce.
questions.explanation: reduce folds every element into the accumulator starting from zero, producing the sum 1518. The initial value is the seed, not an extra element. Carrying the operation through gives 1518; common slips include taking only the first element and omitting the last element.
questions.hint: The accumulator starts at the supplied initial value.

questions.subject: JAVASCRIPT
questions.learningObjective: Interpret JavaScript behavior demonstrated by a short executable snippet involving arrays — foreach.

options.misconception: Only the first callback runs in their view
Confusing count with accumulated total
Skipping the middle element

questions.explanation: forEach calls the callback once per element, adding each to sum, which reaches 1502. forEach returns undefined but the closure updates the outer variable. Working through the snippet, the printed result is 1502.
questions.hint: The callback runs once for every array element.

questions.subject: JAVASCRIPT
questions.learningObjective: Interpret JavaScript behavior demonstrated by a short executable snippet involving strings — charat.

options.misconception: Reading the final digit
Reading index zero instead of one
Choosing the next digit instead

questions.explanation: charAt returns the character at the given zero-based index; index 1 of '1497' is '4'. Index zero would be the first digit, not the second. Working through the snippet, the printed result is 4.
questions.hint: String positions start counting at zero.

questions.subject: JAVASCRIPT
questions.learningObjective: Interpret JavaScript behavior demonstrated by a short executable snippet involving strings — slice.

stimulus.body: A program is processing the value 1498.

options.misconception: Keeping the removed first character
Assuming slice copies the whole string
Stopping after one character

questions.explanation: With one argument, slice returns everything from that index to the end, dropping the first character of '1498'. The result is '498'. Run line by line, the closing console.log emits 498.
questions.hint: A single slice index means from there to the end.

questions.subject: JAVASCRIPT
questions.learningObjective: Interpret JavaScript behavior demonstrated by a short executable snippet involving strings — split join.

options.misconception: Counting a separator after the last digit
Ignoring the inserted separators
Dropping a digit from the count

questions.explanation: split turns '1499' into 4 characters and join inserts a dash between each pair, giving 7 characters. There are one fewer separators than digits. The engine reaches the last line with 7 ready to print.
questions.hint: Count the dashes between digits, not after the last one.
